market_context: United States and Canada; practical, safety-first household guidance written natively for North American readers.
title: How Long Do Eggs Last in the Refrigerator?

seo.title: How Long Do Eggs Last in the Refrigerator?
seo.meta_description: How long eggs keep in the refrigerator, how to store them in their carton, and why handling recommendations differ between markets.
seo.search_intent: Know how long refrigerated eggs keep and apply the recommendation according to market handling, refrigeration history, and carton dates.

excerpt: Shell eggs can keep for several weeks refrigerated, but the cold chain, local market practices, and package guidance matter more than one isolated number.
content_html:
Shell eggs can keep for several weeks in the refrigerator, but storage guidance depends on the market and handling system. In the United States, where commercial shell eggs are washed and sold refrigerated, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) says to keep them at 40°F or below and use them within about three weeks for best quality; federal storage charts commonly show roughly 4 to 5 weeks of refrigerated storage.

The cold chain matters more than one number

If you bought eggs refrigerated, keep them refrigerated. Avoid leaving them on the counter for long periods and repeatedly moving them between warm and cold conditions.

Keep them in the carton on an inside shelf

The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) advises storing eggs in their carton on a refrigerator shelf rather than in the door. Door compartments experience more temperature fluctuation each time the refrigerator is opened.

Different countries use different systems

Some markets do not wash commercial eggs in the same way and may sell them unrefrigerated. Follow local food-safety guidance and the package instructions rather than assuming the U.S. system applies everywhere.

A date does not make poor storage safe

Discard cracked eggs and be cautious when storage history is unknown or the refrigerator has been too warm. Buy clean, uncracked eggs and keep the refrigerator at a safe temperature.

Cooked eggs have a much shorter window

Hard-cooked eggs, peeled or unpeeled, should generally be used within one week. Cooked dishes containing egg generally fall under the shorter refrigerated-leftovers window of about 3 to 4 days.

For raw shell eggs, think in weeks rather than days, but keep them cold and follow the date and guidance that apply where you live.

faq.question: Should eggs be stored in the refrigerator door?
faq.answer: Not in a typical home refrigerator. An inside shelf has more stable temperature.

faq.question: How long do hard-boiled eggs last?
faq.answer: FDA guidance is about one week refrigerated.

faq.question: Do eggs need refrigeration in every country?
faq.answer: Commercial handling practices vary, so follow local food-safety guidance and the package label.
